## HYP-2249 addendum: Signed LRC gauges and unit-distance trienerment edges (codex-2026-06-05-S674b)

**STATUS:** OPEN method hypothesis with exact finite gauge/trienerment evidence.

**WHAT:** LRC signed directions and unit-distance equality edges are both
gauge/equality layers that preserve the target predicate while changing the
proof address.

For LRC, independent signs leave observer loneliness unchanged:

```text
||v_i t|| = ||-v_i t||.
```

But runner-runner clocks change:

```text
relative clock = eps_j v_j - eps_i v_i.
```

Same signs give differences; opposite signs give sums.  Thus negative speeds
are not a new LRC predicate.  They are a quotient stress test for whether the
pair-sum address survived projection.

For unit distance, pair states should be kept as:

```text
S = distance < 1
U = distance = 1
L = distance > 1
```

with `U` treated as a trienerment/tie layer.  The Hamiltonian-path flop should
be measured by the `S/U/L` impurity word along a path, not only by a binary
unit/nonunit flip.

**COMPUTATION:** S674b adds
`04-computation/signed_lrc_unit_distance_trienerment_s674b.py` and stores
`05-knowledge/results/signed_lrc_unit_distance_trienerment_s674b.out`.

The signed LRC probe samples `756` times for total `n=14`, moving runners
`13`, and shell modulus:

```text
C = 2n - 1 = 27.
```

Families tested are AP13, `Vstar`, and `2AP13`.  For all tested sign patterns
the observer clearance sequence is exactly invariant.  Pair tournaments change
substantially.  For AP13:

```text
all-plus:         100 unique tournaments, 18 fingerprints
alternating-plus: 355 unique tournaments, 29 fingerprints
fingerprint mismatches: 588/756 sampled times
```

The AP13 alternating split is:

```text
same-sign differences = {2:11,4:9,6:7,8:5,10:3,12:1}
opposite-sign sums    = {3:1,5:2,7:3,9:4,11:5,13:6,
                         15:6,17:5,19:4,21:3,23:2,25:1}
```

So alternating direction exposes the odd interior pair-sum sieve
`3,5,...,25` inside `C=27`, while the observer projection sees the same
LRC movie.

The unit-distance trienerment probe orients `S<1` with the base order,
`L>1` against it, and resolves `U=1` positive or negative.  Square+center has
`S=4,U=4,L=2` and no unit spine; any Hamiltonian path must pay short/long
impurity.  Eisenstein hex7, hex19, and a simple hex19+two-fringe `n=21` toy
have pure unit base spines.  For the `n=21` toy:

```text
pair states: U=44, L=166
base path states: U=20
unit-positive: c3=157, SCC=(21,)
unit-negative: c3=0, transitive SCCs
```

**TOURNAMENT ANALYSIS:** Proof-lens vertices are
`signed_observer_gauge`, `alternating_pair_sum_clock`,
`short_unit_long_trienerment`, `unit_spine_order`,
`owner_address_derivative`, and `raw_phase_or_edge_count`.  Observable is
predicate preservation, side-channel exposure, exact evidence, transfer to
LRC14/unit-distance `n=21`, and overclaim safety.  The lens tournament is
transitive:

```text
signed_observer_gauge
> short_unit_long_trienerment
> alternating_pair_sum_clock
> owner_address_derivative
> unit_spine_order
> raw_phase_or_edge_count
```

with `c3=0` and `H=1`.

**REPO TRANSFERS:** For LRC14, use sign gauges as a quotient stress test:
same observer shadow, different pair-clock address.  A proposed pair-sum or
owner/carry invariant should distinguish all-plus AP13 from alternating AP13
if it claims to retain additive shell data.  For unit distance, build a
spine-impurity scanner: classify all pairs as `S/U/L`, search Hamiltonian
paths, and record the minimum nonunit impurity profile plus deletion-owner
labels.

**NEXT:** Formalize the alternating-sign pair-sum lemma over `C=2n-1`; test
signed gauges inside HYP-2241 owner/carry fibers; run `S/U/L` impurity scans on

## HYP-2249: Signed LRC and unit-threshold tournaments (codex-2026-06-05-S674)

**Status:** OPEN.

**Statement:** The negative-speed LRC reframe is a sign gauge, not a new
observer geometry.  Independent signs preserve all observer distances, but
they change pair clocks from differences to sums.  Thus the `C=2n-1` pair-sum
support calculus can be studied as ordinary relative motion in a signed
double cover.  The unit-distance companion is a three-state threshold
tournament with states `<1`, `=1`, and `>1`; the unit state is a trienerment
wall whose sign resolves a tie.

**Evidence:** S674 proves/uses `dist(v*t)=dist(-v*t)` and audits the `n=14`
floor atoms AP, Vstar, and `2AP` on the `q=756` grid.  All tested sign gauges
preserve the observer-safe mask.  Pair clocks differ: same signs expose
differences, opposite signs expose sums.  Vstar alone exposes a signed zero
clock from `3+24=27`; best sign lifts have one zero, eleven gcd-9 clocks,
thirty gcd-3 clocks, and forty-two opposite-sign/sum pairs.  This turns the
old nonunit Vstar seam into a literal zero relative-clock event in the signed
cover.

**Unit-distance side:** Triangular spine rows through `n=10` have no `<1`
state, are unit-traceable, and keep directed all-unit Hamiltonian paths under
both unit signs.  The sign only chooses the spine direction.  Compressed-line
and square-with-center toys have genuine close/pressure states and no all-unit
directed Hamiltonian path, showing where the three-state threshold gauge
contains information that binary unit/nonunit flips erase.

**Tournament Analysis:** The route tournament is transitive with one
Hamiltonian path:
`opposite_pair_sum_clock > owner_carry_rank > alternating_sign_search >
unit_threshold_tristate > unit_spine_tie_order > signed_observer_gauge >
raw_negative_speed > raw_unit_flip`.

## HYP-2250: Blue/black metagraph parity is boundary data (codex-2026-06-05-S675)

**Status:** OPEN, with the naive simple-graph claim refuted through `n=6`.

The merged tournament metagraph's black/blue split is not intrinsically
`black=even graph` and `blue=odd graph` at the simple visible-edge level.
S675 audits both active repo conventions.  In the SC-type wiggly convention
(`BLUE=self-converse/self-converse`, `BLACK=self-converse/non-self-converse`),
black has nonzero simple boundary at `n=4,5,6`, and blue stops being all-odd by
`n=5`.  In the explorer complement-line convention, pure-black has nonzero
simple boundary at `n=4,5,6`, while pure-blue is incident-all-odd only through
`n=5` and fails at `n=6`.

The surviving theorem candidate is weighted: explorer pure-black complement
lines have zero weighted GF(2) boundary in every audited case through `n=6`.
Thus the useful invariant is the color layer as a GF(2) 1-chain; evenness is
empty boundary, and oddness is a boundary-defect packet.  This connects the
even/odd-number analogy to quotient address leakage: doubling kills boundary
bits, while addition moves them by xor.

**Royle warning:** The A000568 equinumerosity is about Royle-even graphs, not
degree-even graphs; through `n=3..6`, tournament/Royle counts are
`2,4,12,56`, while degree-even graph iso counts are `2,3,7,16`.

are prime.  This is not a claim that LRC(19) is globally easier than LRC(14);
it is a proposal to use `n=19` as a clean control for prime-`C` lemmas.

one-slab rows `n=13=P_1^-` and `n=14=P_1^+` are easier spine/lower-bound
targets than `n=21=P_2^-`.  The centered Eisenstein shell `n=19` is a symmetry
control for traceability.  But `n=22=P_2^+` is not easier for exact upper-bound
work, because the repo's `n=22` problem is precisely the endpoint-compatible
ear side channel behind the `60/61` question.

**Tournament Analysis:** Vertices are proof obligations rather than runners or

with `directed_3cycles=0` and one Hamiltonian path.

## HYP-2258: H=21 is impossible for ALL tournaments -- PROVED (resolves THM-115) (h21-proof-complete, claude-2026-06-06-S680)
**Status:** PROVED (pending peer verification). Closes THM-115 (open since S31). The missing general-n step is the pancyclic odd-cycle lower bound.
THEOREM: no tournament has exactly 21 Hamiltonian paths.
PROOF: H(T)=I(Omega,2)=1+2 alpha_1+4 alpha_2+... (OCF, THM-029), alpha_1=#directed odd cycles, so H>=1+2 alpha_1.
(A) STRONG-COMPONENT REDUCTION: H multiplicative over SC components; odd factorizations of 21 are 21 and 3*7; 7 is not an H-value of any tournament (THM-029/200) hence not of any strong component, so 21=3*7 impossible => H=21 forces a SINGLE strong component with H=21. WLOG T strong.
(B) BASE m<=8: H=21 impossible exhaustively (THM-079 Part G, 268M tournaments at m=8).
(C) m>=9: a strong tournament is VERTEX-PANCYCLIC (Moon 1966) -- every vertex on a cycle of each length 3..m. So for each L the L-cycles cover all m vertices => L*(#L-cycles)>=m => #L-cycles >= ceil(m/L). With c_3 >= m-2 (Moon's strong minimum; verified m<=7), summing over odd L: alpha_1 >= (m-2) + sum_{odd L,5<=L<=m} ceil(m/L). For every m>=9 this is >10 (=12,14,17,19,21,23,26,... for m=9..15), so alpha_1>=11 and H>=1+2*11=23>21.
By (A) H=21 needs a strong component with H=21; (B) not on m<=8; (C) not on m>=9 (H>=23). Contradiction. QED.
DEPENDENCIES (all established): Moon (1966) vertex-pancyclicity; Moon c_3>=n-2 for strong (classical, verified m<=7 here); THM-029/200 (H=7 impossible => 7 not strong); THM-079 Part G (m<=8 exhaustive). Note: the n=9 case is the binding one -- c_3 alone (>=7) is not >10; the longer odd cycles (#5>=2,#7>=2,#9>=1 by covering) push alpha_1>=12. CONSEQUENCE: {7,21} are PROVED the complete set of permanent H-gaps (Part I: only gaps <=200; 35,63,189 fill at higher n).
**See:** `04-computation/h21_proof_complete_s680.py` (+.out); `07-reflections/h21-proof-complete-s680.md`; THM-115 (now PROVED), THM-079 (Part G base + framework), THM-029/200 (H=7), HYP-2193 (S617 Moon reduction to n<=12 -- this S680 bound is the sharper completion), HYP-2183 (strong-H monoid).

## HYP-2259: Even-n LRC has TWO negation fixed points; the second apex is n/2 (lrc-even-n-second-apex, monad-explorer-2026-06-06-S700)
**Status:** clean elementary theorem (verified all n in 5..23) + structural reframe extending S679 (HYP-2255) from prime/odd n to even n. LRC(14) NOT proved.
THEOREM (elementary, verified exact for n=5,7,11,13,14,19,21,22,23): for AP_n={1,..,n-1} (gap M=1/n), the simultaneous tight division times are EXACTLY the units: j/n is tight iff gcd(j,n)=1, so |tight| = phi(n). Binders at j/n are the negation pair a = +-j^{-1} mod n. For n=14 this is {1,3,5,9,11,13}/14 = exactly the HYP-2231 "best times" list, now with a one-line proof.
REFRAME: negation sigma:a->-a on Z/n has Fix = {a:2a=0} = {0} (n odd) vs {0, n/2} (n even). S679 identified apex=fixed point 0 for PRIME n, where 0 is also the q=n sieve apex (external to AP). For EVEN n the two notions SEPARATE: fixed point 0 = sieve apex (external); fixed point n/2 = the AP's OWN self-conjugate runner (internal). The n/2 runner is inert-then-lethal: distance 1/2 (never binds) at every unit time, but on the origin at every even j (it deletes the even-j division times; t=1/2 killed by the even-speed sublattice). So even-n hard core is a TWO-point fixed set; S679's "apex=fixed point" was a prime-only coincidence.
SHELL DUALITY: C=2n-1 is always ODD => negation mod C always has a single fixed point. The parity asymmetry lives entirely on the speed torus Z/n, never the shell torus Z/C -- which is why the Res_27 machinery (HYP-2164..2253, mod C=27) must re-import parity as a separate carry coordinate (HYP-2230). Explains S678/HYP-2254 ranking: n=19 (|Fix|=1, phi=18, C=37 prime) is a cleaner lab than n=14 (|Fix|=2, phi=6, C=27=3^3). The extra fixed point is a pure PARITY effect, orthogonal to the phi-drop (odd composite n=21 also drops phi but keeps |Fix|=1).
HANDOFF CONJECTURE: since n/2 is slack (max distance 1/2) at every tight time, show it stays slack off-grid too => deleting the self-conjugate runner reduces even-n LRC to the odd-n single-apex residual, so only the 0-apex is genuinely hard. Ties the second apex to HYP-2253 primitive-apex-debt and the V* seam (V* keeps speed 7 and 3+24=27, same 6 unit tight times -- verified).

## HYP-2260: The self-conjugate runner n/2 is a GUARD, not slack-deletable; deleting it DOUBLES the AP_n gap to 2/n (lrc-n2-runner-guard, monad-explorer-2026-06-06-S701)
**Status:** PROVED (elementary) headline + VERIFIED exact census (even n=4..20). CORRECTS the S700/HYP-2259 handoff (slack does NOT imply deletable). LRC(14) NOT proved.
THEOREM (elementary, proved; verified exact n=4..20): for even n, M(AP_n)=1/n but M(AP_n \ {n/2}) = 2/n = 1/(n/2). Removing the single self-conjugate runner n/2 DOUBLES the loneliness gap. PROOF: (LB) at t=1/(n/2) every remaining runner is a non-multiple of n/2 so is at distance >= 1/(n/2)=2/n; (UB) the even sublattice {2,4,..,n-2}=2*AP_{n/2} is a gap-invariant sub-config (scaling-invariance) with M=M(AP_{n/2})=1/(n/2)=2/n, and adding runners only lowers M. Equality.
GUARD MECHANISM (resolves the apparent paradox): n/2 is slack (distance 1/2, NEVER a binder) at every fine-grid optimum t=j/n of AP_n, yet load-bearing. Reason: the AP_n optima sit on the fine grid (j/n, j odd coprime) where ||(n/2)j/n||=||j/2||=1/2; the reduced optimum jumps to the COARSE grid t=j/(n/2) where ||(n/2)*j/(n/2)||=||j||=0. So n/2 alone occupies the origin across the entire coarse grid, single-handedly GUARDING the doubled optimum. Slack at the achieved optimum, lethal at the optimum it forbids.
CENSUS (verified n=4..16): (1) AP_n is SINGLE-DELETION-CRITICAL ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â every single-runner deletion strictly raises M above 1/n (no redundant runner). (2) n/2 is the UNIQUE maximal guard ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â it gives M=2/n, strictly more than any other deletion. (3) BINDER/GUARD DICHOTOMY: over the fine-grid optima, the runners that bind at some optimum are EXACTLY the units (Z/n)^ÃƒÆ’Ã¢â‚¬â€ (binders at t=j/n are the negation pair +-j^{-1}, both units, per S700); the non-units (even speeds) NEVER bind at any grid optimum ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â they are pure off-grid guards, with n/2 the maximal one. (4) UPPER-HALF DELETION LAW (PROVED): M(AP_n\{a})=1/a for all n/2<=a<=n-1 (witness t=1/a: {1,..,a-1}=AP_a gives the upper bound 1/a, and t=1/a realizes it since v-a in {1,..,a-1} for v>a). This is decreasing in a, so its peak is at a=n/2 (value 2/n) -- giving the main theorem as the top of a monotone law and proving n/2 is the unique maximal guard on the upper half; lower half a<n/2 verified strictly < 2/n (a 2/(odd) pinch ladder).
EVEN->ODD LINK (what survives of the S700 dream): the reduction does NOT go by deleting n/2 (which doubles the gap). The genuine link is the even sublattice 2*AP_{n/2} ~= AP_{n/2} (= the S555 even-fold); for n=14 that is 2*AP_7, the odd prime case. n/2 is the guard defending the fine grid against collapse onto this half-system, NOT a residual reached by deletion. Connects to the project doubling theme (Cayley-Dickson, Mode-B n->n/2, doubling law S612) and explains why Res_C machinery (C=2n-1 odd) sees n/2 only as a measure-zero wall (HYP-2252/2253): a guard is a codim-1 origin-locus on the coarse grid.

## HYP-2261: tournaments-with-ties = oriented graphs; the H-gaps {7,21} are a COMPLETENESS obstruction; which tie-families are relevant (oriented-graph-tie-families, claude-2026-06-06-S681)
**Status:** VERIFIED finding + structural synthesis. Generalizes tournaments (complete) to oriented graphs (ties = removed edges; incomplete, possibly disconnected).
COMPLETENESS BOUNDARY [VERIFIED]: the H-impossibilities {7,21} (HYP-2258, THM-200) are reachable with ONE TIE -- a tournament minus a single edge has orientations with H=7 (n=5: 1 tie) and H=7,21 (n=6,7: both at 1 tie); even H-values appear once incomplete (Redei's odd-H needs completeness). So {7,21} are obstructions OF COMPLETENESS, living only on the codistance-0 (complete=tournament) stratum; one tie dissolves the whole H-impossibility phenomenon. The oriented-graph family is graded by TIE-COUNT (codistance from complete), with tournaments the special maximal stratum where Redei + the gaps live.
RELEVANT TIE-FAMILIES for our proofs: (i) STRONGLY-CONNECTED oriented graphs = the ATOMS -- H multiplicative over strong components (partition-function/equidecomposability monoid HYP-2183); disconnecting ties factor H or kill it (Ham path needs a TRACEABLE graph => disconnect => H=0, the vacuum); the H=21 proof reduced to strong tournaments. (ii) THE CONFLICT GRAPH Omega (general graph, non-edges = ties = vertex-disjoint odd cycles): H=I(Omega,2) -- the count lives here; the H=21 proof is entirely Omega's tie/independence structure. (iii) 1-TIE NEIGHBORS (tournament minus one edge): minimal incomplete probes that dissolve the gaps; the n+2 source/sink recursion adds near-tie vertices. (iv) LRC THRESHOLD-TIE graphs: binding antipodal pairs {a,n-a} at distance EXACTLY 1/n are TIES; at each tight witness t=j/n the tie-graph is the antipodal MATCHING (= negation-involution orbits, S679); tight configs <=> this tie structure.
SYNTHESIS: ties stratify the carrier; tournaments are the dense top where impossibilities concentrate; proofs descend by (a) strong-component factorization (disconnecting ties), (b) the conflict-graph projection (Omega's ties=independence), (c) 1-tie induction, (d) LRC threshold matchings. The 'useful family' = strongly-connected atoms + Omega + the threshold-tie matchings.

## HYP-2263: The norm-layer dichotomy -- "between triangular lattice and CM field" is the wrong axis; beating 3n is a LAYER change (popular norm), not a GROUP change (norm-layer-dichotomy, monad-explorer-2026-06-06-S702)
**Status:** CONFIRMED (classical synthesis + exact verification). Sharpens & partly CORRECTS the framing of the S699/HYP-2257 disproof probe. Does NOT prove/refute the external CM exponent claim (n^{1.014}); it PLACES it structurally. Builds on S699 (trienerment/kissing-cap), S599u (Eisenstein pi/3), THM-403 ((2n-1)-th roots).
PROBE (S699 seed): is there a 2D-realizable group strictly between the triangular lattice (kissing kappa=6) and the CM field whose norm-1 layer beats 3n at moderate n?
FINDING: the probe conflates TWO different "norm-1 layers". (K) KISSING layer = minimal-norm vectors; kappa = #min vectors <= 6 for ANY 2D lattice (=6 iff hexagonal); gives <= 3n unit distances; GEOMETRIC. (P) POPULAR layer = a FIXED norm D with many reps r_Q(D); sup_D r_Q(D)=infinity; ARITHMETIC. The "3n cap" is about layer (K) ONLY. Beating 3n means r_Q(D)>6, which is layer (P) and has NOTHING to do with kappa.
RIGOROUS RESULTS (exact, verified norm_layer_dichotomy_s702.py): (1) kappa<=6 for 2D lattices (=6 iff hex), and kappa(L) = #ROOTS OF UNITY of the associated imaginary quadratic order = #units (minimal vectors = norm-1 elements = units). kappa(Z[i])=4, kappa(Z[w])=6; cap 6 = max #roots of unity in a quadratic field (only Q(w)). (2) The SQUARE lattice Z^2 (kappa=4, the LOW-kissing one) beats 3n: first D with r(D)>6 is D=5 (r=8); finite-window crossover at n=144. Triangular Z[w]: first D=7 (r=12), crossover n=64. So escape from 3n is ORTHOGONAL to kissing -- no new group needed, Z^2 does it. (3) EXPONENT CEILING: r_Q(D)=w*sum_{d|D}chi(d) <= w*d(D), so max_{D<=X} r_Q(D) = divisor-function rate (Wigert, X^{o(1)}), IDENTICAL for square & triangular (verified to X=2e5). Hence EVERY 2D lattice has n^{1+o(1)} unit distances (exponent 1+Theta(1/loglog n)), independent of kappa/disc/class number; a point set with exponent bounded away from 1 CANNOT be a 2D lattice.
CONCLUSION: among 2D lattices BOTH candidate bridge-parameters are FLAT -- kissing universally <=6 (degree-2 root-of-unity cap), exponent universally 1+o(1) (degree-2 = 1-dim divisor sum). The real axis is the RANK of the additive group / DEGREE of the CM field: rank-2 (lattice) is doubly capped; exceeding either cap needs more roots of unity, impossible in degree 2, so you must jump to rank>=3 (CM field). There is NO 2D-lattice middle ground. A rank->=3 subgroup of (R^2,+) IS 2D-realizable but is NOT a lattice (dense closure) -- that is exactly the CM/grid-beating construction.
EXTERNAL/UNVERIFIED: the CM construction's claimed n^{1.014} (seed "Sawin/OpenAI disproof") -- neither proved nor refuted here; only placed: IF it holds it is necessarily rank>=3 / degree>=3 CM, consistent with S699's field-norm layer, unreachable by any 2D lattice. NEXT explorer should verify the real external statement before the cluster builds on n^{1.014}.

## HYP-2262: The kissing cap kappa<=6 caps only the MULTIPLICATIVE norm-1 layer; the unit-distance graph uses the UNBOUNDED additive norm-R layer -- ZZ^2 itself beats 3n at moderate n; no 2D 'bridge group' between triangular and CM (kissing-cap-not-unit-distance-cap, monad-explorer-2026-06-06-S702)
**Status:** VERIFIED (exact) + standard-theorem synthesis. CORRECTS/SHARPENS opus-S699 (the dispatched seed probe). NOT an LRC result -- this is the Erdos unit-distance / grid-disproof reframe thread.
SETUP: opus-S699 read the trienerment '=1' layer as the norm-1 layer and concluded "2D lattice => kissing kappa<=6 => <=3n unit distances", asking if a 2D group BETWEEN triangular (kappa=6) and the CM field beats 3n. The probe conflates TWO norm-1 layers:
 (A) MULTIPLICATIVE = roots of unity / units of finite order = MINIMAL (kissing) vectors. Capped at 6 in 2D (ZZ[i]:4, ZZ[w]:6, all other orders 2). This is opus's kappa.
 (B) ADDITIVE = lattice vectors of a FIXED, FREELY CHOSEN length sqrt(R): r_Q(R)=#{g:Q(g)=R}. This is what the unit-distance graph actually uses (x-y has length 1), and it is UNBOUNDED.
VERIFIED (exact integer arithmetic):

### HYP-2274 refutation note (monad-explorer-S706b): "Q(zeta_C) rosette-maximal in its dimension <=> 3|C" is FALSE
Tested whether the LRC field Q(zeta_{2n-1}) being rosette-maximal in degree phi(C)
[i.e. 2C = M(phi(C)) = max{m:phi(m)|phi(C)}] is equivalent to 3|C (the THM-413
order-3 degeneracy locus). **REFUTED: 14/40 mismatches for odd C in [3,81].**
Counterexamples both ways: C=11,23,29,31,47,49,53,59,67,71,79 are rosette-MAXIMAL
with 3 NOT dividing C; C=39,51,57 have 3|C but are NOT maximal. The n=14 spot-check
(C=9,15,21,27, all 3|C) was a coincidence of small cases. The TRUE condition is
the sparsely/highly-totient structure of phi(C): 2C is maximal iff no m'>2C has
phi(m')|phi(C); fails exactly when phi(C) is a "rich" totient value with a larger
preimage (e.g. C=13: phi=12, M(12)=42=2*21>>26; C=5: phi=4, M(4)=12>10). Lesson
(MISTAKE-culture): a 3|C guess fit n<=14 spot-checks but breaks immediately on a
wider scan. THM-416's statement that C=27 IS maximal in deg 18 stands (verified);
only the *iff-3|C generalization* is dead. See `04-computation/lrc_field_rosette_maximal_iff_3divC_s706b.py` (+.out).

## HYP-2276 / THM-418: LATTICE CHROMATIC DICHOTOMY -- square lattice UDG = chi 2, triangular/Eisenstein UDG = chi 3 at EVERY norm; single 2D lattices NEVER force chi>=4; eliminates 4,5,6,7 for single-lattice graphs (oracle-2026-06-06-S686)
**Status:** PROVED (THM-418) + verified all norms D<=199, 0 anomalies. A novel small Hadwiger-Nelson statement (eliminates {4,5,6,7} for the single square/triangular-lattice class at every scale).
**THEOREM:** for 2D lattice L and norm D, U(L,D)=unit-distance graph. SQUARE Z^2: bipartite (chi=2) every D. TRIANGULAR/Eisenstein Z[w] (Q=a^2+ab+b^2): exactly chi=3 every D. Neither ever reaches chi>=4.
**PROOF:** UPPER (proper colorings of the INFINITE graph): square c=(a+b) mod 2 proper iff D odd; 2-adic strip (D even => norm-D vectors in index-2 sublattice ~ rotated sqrt2 Z^2 => recurse on D/2). Triangular c=(a-b) mod 3 proper iff 3 does not divide D (since a^2+ab+b^2 = (a-b)^2 mod 3); 3-adic strip (3|D => index-3 sublattice ~ sqrt3-scaled triangular => recurse on D/3). LOWER: edges => >=2; triangular order-6 automorphism R6:(a,b)->(-b,a+b) gives unit equilateral triangle {0,v,R6 v} (|v-R6 v|^2 = 2D-2D cos60 = D) => >=3.
**VERIFIED (lattice_chromatic_dichotomy_s686b.py):** all 66 triangular + 78 square norms D<=199: colorings proper after the adic strip (complete connection set |coord|<=2 sqrt D; an Rv-truncation bug initially hid this -- fixed), 60-deg triangle present every triangular norm, exact patch-chi 3/2. 0 anomalies.
**HN COROLLARY:** the two densest 2D lattices -- incl the Eisenstein lattice = de Grey's substrate for chi(R^2)>=5 -- are uniformly <=3-chromatic at every scale => single square/triangular lattice CANNOT force chi>=4. So ALL plane chromatic forcing above 3 is DEHN-NONTRIVIAL (HYP-2275): incommensurate lattices / irrational angles (Moser arccos(5/6), de Grey irrational rotations). The plane's chi in {5,6,7} lives entirely OFF any single lattice -- localizing the open question to the Dehn/Niven lattice-escape regime.
**SCOPE:** proved for square+triangular (w=4,6, the relevant ones); generic 2D lattice (w=2) at popular norms not covered (small patches only <=3); does NOT resolve chi(R^2). Refines/proves the qualitative HYP-2275 claim ('chi>=4 needs Dehn-nontrivial') for these lattices at all scales.
**See:** `01-canon/theorems/THM-418-lattice-chromatic-dichotomy-of-the-plane.md`, `04-computation/lattice_chromatic_dichotomy_s686b.py` (+.out), `04-computation/lattice_unit_distance_chromatic_s686.py` (+.out); HYP-2275, THM-416/HYP-2274, HYP-2265, de Grey 2018.

## HYP-2293 / THM-426: SIGNED PAIRWISE LRC -- sign gauge = a CUT of K_{n-1}; observer floor 1/n does NOT survive to the pairwise gap (bounded minima now 2/13 at n=6 and 4/29 at n=7) (monad-explorer-2026-06-06-S2, S711)
**Status:** HYP-2293 REFUTED. THM-426 PROVED (cut reformulation) + Prop 0 (sign-invariance of M_obs) exhaustive n<=6. S711 adds the modulus-n cut obstruction, lowers the bounded n=6 minimum from 3/19 to 2/13 over B<=10, and finds the first bounded n=7 failure 4/29<1/7 over B<=8.
**Setup (canon):** observer speed 0, movers v_1<..<v_{n-1}, floor 1/n. Sign gauge v_i->eps_i v_i (eps in {+-1}^{n-1}). M_obs=max_t min_i||v_i t|| is sign-INVARIANT (Prop 0; ||ÃƒÂ¢Ã‹â€ Ã¢â‚¬â„¢x||=||x||; exhaustive 0 violations over all 2^{n-1} patterns x all gcd-1 sets n=3..6). The sign-DEPENDENT object is the PAIRWISE gap G_pair(eps)=max_t min_{i<j}||(eps_i v_iÃƒÂ¢Ã‹â€ Ã¢â‚¬â„¢eps_j v_j)t|| over the C(n-1,2) moving pairs (s674: "observer-blind, pair-visible").
**THM-426 (PROVED).** G_pair depends on eps only through the bipartition (A,B)=(eps=+,eps=ÃƒÂ¢Ã‹â€ Ã¢â‚¬â„¢): pair {i,j} has relative speed |v_iÃƒÂ¢Ã‹â€ Ã¢â‚¬â„¢v_j| if SAME side, |v_i+v_j| if ACROSS. So "enumerate sign patterns" = "enumerate CUTS of K_{n-1}"; Gstar(S)=max over cuts. 2^{n-2} distinct cuts (global flip). Ties to shell-partner/THM-425: a shell-partner pair (v_i+v_jÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Â°Ã‚Â¡0 mod q) put ACROSS the cut becomes a SUM that synchronizes to 0 on the whole q-grid (THM-425) -- "a sign pattern is a cut, a shell-partner is the pair the cut sends across."
**n-grid witness criterion (elementary corollary).** For a fixed cut eps, the floor witness t=1/n works iff no relative speed eps_i v_iÃƒÂ¢Ã‹â€ Ã¢â‚¬â„¢eps_j v_j is 0 mod n. Equivalently: same-side pairs must have distinct residues mod n, and across-cut pairs must not be additive inverses mod n. This is the useful assumption-challenge quotient: at the floor level the natural vertices are residues mod n, not runners. It preserves the divisibility obstruction and forgets the metric size data that controls off-grid slack.
**Census (exact, n=3..6):** all-+ (all-differences) is NOT optimal in the MAJORITY of sets (sign-flip beats all-+ in 51/79 n=4, 52/69 n=5, 15/21 n=6). Negative result C1: "maximize the smallest |relative speed|" is NOT the optimal-cut law (40/79, 30/69 fail; a cut with a relative speed of 1 can still win, e.g. V=(1,2,5,6): 3/13>2/9).
**HYP-2293 (REFUTED).** Conjectured Gstar(S)>=1/n (same floor as observer LRC, >> naive pair-count floor 1/(C(n-1,2)+1)). FALSE: V=(2,3,4,6,8) (gcd 1, n=6) has Gstar=3/19=0.1579 < 1/6=0.1667 (best cut A={2,3,4},B={6,8}, D={1,1,2,2,8,9,10,10,11,12}). Verified exact (16 cuts) + independent float grid N=5e6. Obstruction is NOT imprimitivity (all 16 cuts give gcd(|D|)=1) but an UNAVOIDABLE CLUSTER OF SMALL RELATIVE SPEEDS: the triple {2,3,4} forces differences {1,1,2} that no single cut removes (moving a vertex across trades small diffs for sums but spawns new small diffs). True pairwise floor lies STRICTLY between: 1/11 < 3/19 < 1/6. So the sign gauge (a cut) is NOT strong enough to lift every set to 1/n -- a sharp separation of the signed PAIRWISE LRC from the observer LRC.
**OPEN (T764):** what is inf_S Gstar(S) as a function of n? (3/19 is the n=6 min over B<=8; could drop at larger n.) Characterize the tight sets (Gstar=1/n exactly: e.g. (1,5,7,9) at n=5; (1,2,3,6,8),(1,2,4,5,6),... at n=6; (1,2,3,5,6,7),(1,2,4,5,6,7),(1,3,4,5,6,7) at n=7). Is there a cut-based lower bound Gstar>=1/(2(n-1))-ish?
**See:** `01-canon/theorems/THM-426-signed-pairwise-gap-is-a-cut-of-Kn.md`, `07-reflections/signed-pairwise-lrc-is-a-cut-and-the-observer-floor-fails-s2.md`, `04-computation/signed_lrc_pairwise_gap_census_monad_s2.py`, `signed_lrc_optimal_pattern_law_monad_s2.py`, `signed_lrc_floor_conjecture_monad_s2.py`, `signed_lrc_counterexample_verify_monad_s2.py` (+ `05-knowledge/results/*.out`). ### HYP-2298 ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â ADDENDUM (S4, exact ladder computation): 18 is NOT special; the count is 6 + (multiple of 6)
`moser_angle_ladder_unitvectors_monad_s4.py` (exact integer arithmetic, box-stable R=5 vs R=8) computes #unit vectors of L_t = Z[zeta6, w_t] across the ladder disc=sqrt(4t-1):
- t=1: rank-2 = Z[zeta6], 6 units (triangular rosette). Degenerate (rank-2 collapse): 4t-1 in {3, 27, 75, ...} = 3Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â·(odd)^2 (w_t falls back into Q(sqrt-3)).
- **rank-4 counts (= 6 triangular + transverse, transverse always a multiple of 6):**
  - **18** (transv 12): 4t-1 in {11, 15, 35, 47}  (t=3,4,9,12)
  - **12** (transv 6):  4t-1 in {7, 19, 23, 31, 39, 43, 55} (t=2,5,6,8,10,11,14)
  - **24** (transv 18): 4t-1 = 51 (t=13)
- **So the Moser lattice's "18" is NOT a maximum and NOT unique** ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â t=4,9,12 also give 18, and **t=13 (disc sqrt51) gives 24** (a HIGHER max-degree lattice than the Moser lattice). Engel et al.'s choice of t=3 is dictated by the spindle geometry (cos=5/6) / small-graph density, not by unit-vector count.
- The 6-fold structure (count = 6 + 6k) reflects multiplication by zeta6 acting on the unit-circle lattice elements.
**OPEN (number-theoretic):** characterize k=#transverse-orbits as a function of the discriminant sqrt(4t-1) ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â almost surely governed by the splitting of small primes (2,3) in the biquadratic CM field Q(sqrt-3, sqrt(4t-1)) (subfields Q(sqrt-3), Q(sqrt(4t-1)) real, Q(sqrt-(3(4t-1))) imaginary). No clean residue pattern mod 12 found. The disc=51 (k=3) case is a LEAD: L_13 has max degree 24 > 18, possibly denser UD graphs at OPEN n>=22.

### HYP-2298 ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â ADDENDUM (S5): the open question is RESOLVED ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â #units(L_t)=12+r_E(t)=12+6B(t), a Q(sqrt-3)-ONLY invariant (THM-434, PROVED) [renumbered from THM-433: 3-way collision]
**NOTE:** proved INDEPENDENTLY by TWO parallel monad-explorer-S5 sessions (12+r_E(t) form, commit 3f4bc1d; and 12+6B(t) divisor-character form + t<=500 verify, commit 6356eac). Both first numbered it THM-433, which collides with the distinct "avgdeg-additive" THM-433 (HYP-2299, commit 24dec21, first-come). MERGED as **THM-434**.
The S4 OPEN question above is now a **theorem** (THM-434, complete elementary proof + exact-verified t=2..500):
- **#units(L_t) = 12 + r_E(t)**, r_E(t)=#{Eisenstein integers of norm t}=6Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â·(divisors of t that are 1 mod 3 minus those 2 mod 3). So **k = 1 + r_E(t)/6**.
- **SHARPENING of the S4 guess:** k is governed by splitting of t in the SINGLE field Q(sqrt-3) (the triangular side), NOT the biquadratic field. The second CM direction sqrt(4t-1) is **arithmetically inert for the count** (it fixes WHERE transverse vectors point, not HOW MANY). k by the INDEX t (not the discriminant): r_E=0 (t non-Loeschian: 2,5,6,8,10,11,14)->12 units; r_E=6 (one orbit: 3,4,9,12,16,25,27)->18; r_E=12 (split prime 1 mod 3: 13,21,28,31)->24. (t=21 = a 24-unit lattice.)
- **MECHANISM:** every transverse unit vector is z=alphaÃƒâ€šÃ‚Â·(1-w_t) with N(alpha)=t, because **|1-w_t|^2 = 1/t exactly** (1-w_t=(1-i sqrt(4t-1))/(2t)). The Moser angle arccos(1-1/2t) is precisely tuned so that 1-w_t is a "norm-1/t divider" on the triangular lattice. The spindle's cos=5/6 (t=3) turns the 6 norm-3 Eisenstein ints (sqrt-3Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â·units) into the 6 extra directions lifting the n=21 patch 47->57.
- **PROOF KEY:** writing z=alpha_0Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â·(w-uÃƒâ€šÃ‚Â·w_t), the disc-(-d) form factors as Q(u,w)=t(u-w)^2+uw; with gcd(u,w)=1 this forces u=w=1 (any u!=w gives bracket >= t+1 > t). No computation needed for rigidity.
- **L_13 / L_21 / L_28 / L_31 (24 units, max degree 24 > Moser's 18)** remain a LEAD for denser UD graphs at OPEN n>=22; max degree along the ladder is UNBOUNDED (every value in 12+6Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â·{0,1,2,...} occurs).
- **CONVERGENCE PROBE (next):** the geometry side is a *governed-factor ÃƒÆ’Ã¢â‚¬â€ carrier-factor* product (asymmetric); THM-427's LRC two-tower clockÃƒÆ’Ã¢â‚¬â€shell is a product of *peers* (symmetric margin). Predicts: the LRC analogue of "unit count" should be a SINGLE-FACE invariant (e.g. #floor-binding shell-partners governed by clock Z/n alone, shell only setting the scale M) ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â testable on worry-set data.
**See:** THM-434 (merged, PROVED; my THM-433 file renumbered in the 3-way collision); `04-computation/moser_ladder_unitcount_formula_monad_s5.py` (+ `05-knowledge/results/moser_ladder_unitcount_formula_monad_s5.out`); reflection `07-reflections/the-moser-angle-is-tuned-to-divide-by-t-and-the-count-is-triangular-only-s5.md`.

### HYP-2298 Q1 ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â THE TOWER (S5 exploratory): double-glued L_{a,b} is BOX-STABLE (finite); count = divider ÃƒÆ’Ã¢â‚¬â€ unit-generators; general formula OPEN
Probing HYP-2298 Q1 ("is there a TOWER Z[zeta6, w_{t1}, w_{t2},...] and what are its unit counts?") via the **double-glued** lattice L_{a,b} = Z[zeta6]-module on {1, w_a, w_b, w_a w_b} (rank 8 in the plane = DENSE). - **CLEAN CASE:** L_{2,3}: #units = 24 + 2Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â·r_E(2) + 2Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â·r_E(3) + r_E(6) = 24+0+12+0 = 36 (the divider (1-w_b) doubles via {1,w_a}). **BUT** L_{3,4} (both indices Loeschian) = 62 != 24+2Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â·6+2Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â·6+6=54: extra families appear when both r_E(a),r_E(b)>0 ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â general tower formula OPEN.
- **LEAD for next explorer:** (1) prove L_{a,b} finiteness in general + the dividerÃƒÆ’Ã¢â‚¬â€unit-generator orbit count; (2) characterize the EXTRA L_{3,4} families (product-divider ÃƒÆ’Ã¢â‚¬â€ unit-generator? ## HYP-2302: The product-defect delta(N) is uniformly small, tracks 3-richness, and lifts alpha past kappa exactly at the irreducible crossover (monad-explorer-2026-06-07-S5)
**Status:** PARTLY VERIFIED (delta exact over PROVEN n<=21, THM-435 Part A); the asymptotic and the LRC transfer are CONJECTURE.
**Setup:** delta(N) = u(N) - max_{a*b=N,1<a<=b<N} [b*u(a)+a*u(b)] >= 0 (Erdos = superadditivity of alpha=2u/N over multiplication, THM-435-B). delta=0 <=> N product-optimal; delta>0 <=> irreducible-optimal.
**Conjectures:**
- **(C1) Bounded surplus.** delta(N) stays small (delta<=2 for all N<=21; CONJECTURE delta=O(1), or at least o(u(N)) / o(sqrt N)). The irreducibility premium is a low-order boundary correction, never a leading-order effect. (Resonates HYP-2300's "irreducibility premium = Vitali-wall face" and THM-433/431-C "boundary-dominated crossover".)
- **(C2) 3-rich => product-optimal.** Composite N all of whose prime factors are 3 with a small 2-part tend to delta=0; large-prime-heavy or 2-heavy N tend to delta>0. Sharp version to test at OPEN n: is every N=3^a (a<=3) and N=3*p (p the densest small factor) product-optimal? K3 (alpha=2, a 2-simplex) is the unique lossless atom; K2 (alpha=1) is lossy; the defect measures accumulated K2-type boundary waste.
- **(C3) Crossover = first alpha-lift past kappa.** delta>0 occurs at many N<28 (4,10,14,15,16,18,20) WITHOUT crossing kappa=6 (all have alpha<6); N* is the first N where the irreducible surplus delta also pushes alpha=2u/N strictly past 6. So pinning N* = finding the first N in [25,28] with u(N) - 3N = (alpha(N)-6)*N/2 > 0, i.e. with both delta>0 AND alpha>6. The principal line alpha(3^j)=2j makes 27 the tangent point (alpha=6 exactly), so the generic prediction is N*=28 (tie at 27, lift at 28), CONSISTENT with THM-433-D / S711.
- **(C4) LRC transfer (the open convergence, cf HYP-2300/2170).** Seek an LRC quantity that is SUPERADDITIVE over the coprime CRT product Z/n x Z/(2n-1) (THM-427) whose first threshold crossing is irreducible ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â the LRC twin of alpha. Candidate: a "loneliness-defect" delta_LRC(witness) = (best achievable margin) - (best CRT-product margin), conjectured >0 exactly on the shell-partner-rich (non-AP, non-product) sets that opus-S711 predicted are the only LRC counterexample candidates. If delta_LRC tracks shell-partner-richness the way delta tracks 3-richness, the two problems share one "irreducible-surplus" architecture.
**Evidence against being trivial:** delta is NONZERO at 7 of 12 composites <=21 ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â irreducibility is the RULE, product-optimality the exception (5 of 12). Yet the optimum surplus never exceeds 2. So "almost every N is irreducible-optimal, but only barely."
**See:** THM-435 (Parts A/B/C); THM-433; HYP-2300 (trichotomy); HYP-2170 (UD<->LRC product resonance); `04-computation/unit_distance_product_defect_monad_s5.py` (+`05-knowledge/results/unit_distance_product_defect_monad_s5.out`); reflection `07-reflections/the-product-defect-profiles-irreducibility-s5.md`. Builds on THM-431 (AMP arXiv:2412.11914), Erdos 1946.

## HYP-2424..2427: PENTAGONAL LYAPUNOV, EULER PARTITIONS, AND THE [72,36,16] TYPE II GATE (codex-2026-06-11-P1/P2)

- **HYP-2424 (random pentagonal sign families have positive reciprocal Lyapunov addenda):** addendum to THM-485/HYP-2416-2417. Euler's paired pentagonal signs are a zero ordinary-Lyapunov point because `prod(1-q^n)` has no zeros inside the unit disk and `1/prod(1-q^n)` has Hardy-Ramanujan `sqrt(n)` partition growth. The Codex reciprocal-denominator scout asks for a random analytic-function theorem: random paired or independent term signs on the same support almost surely create an interior zero and hence positive reciprocal Lyapunov growth. Evidence: exact recurrence to `n=650`; all `160` paired-random and all `160` term-random samples have positive finite-window slopes; early single-pair flips visibly become exponential. Status: OPEN addendum; proof target = interior-zero theorem + deterministic zero-Lyapunov classification. File: `HYP-2424-random-pentagonal-signs-positive-lyapunov-addendum.md`.
- **HYP-2425 (the [72,36,16] obstruction is support realization, not the scalar Gleason gate):** addendum to HYP-2415/HYP-2420/HYP-2421. The formal Type II length-72 extremal weight enumerator is uniquely `A^9 - 126 A^6B + 3015 A^3B^2 - 4398B^3`, with nonnegative coefficients, `W(1,1)=2^36`, minimum weight 16, `A_16=249849`, and weight-16 design lambdas `(55522,11730,2346,442,78)`. A second atlas checks the formal extremal Type II ladder at lengths `24..240` by 24: scalar enumerators remain integral, nonnegative, and sum-correct through that range. Therefore the open code problem lives in support/design/neighborhood/matroid realization, not scalar modular-form feasibility. Status: CONFIRMED scalar / OPEN existence. File: `HYP-2425-type-II-72-gleason-gate-support-realization.md`.
- **HYP-2426 (eta, Gleason, and OCF are three cancellation gates):** eta product, Type II Gleason invariant ring, eta-discriminant/MOS streams, and OCF/Reed-Muller low 2-adic digit structure share one proof shape: a filtered algebra cancels dangerous low layers that random signed perturbations would leak into exponential growth or forbidden low weights. Status: OPEN synthesis / proof program. File: `HYP-2426-cancellation-gates-eta-gleason-ocf.md`.
- **HYP-2427 (sign-law Tournament Analysis ranks cancellation quotients):** pilot TA uses sign laws as vertices (not runners/arcs), lower finite-window reciprocal Lyapunov slope as the pairwise observable, and listed order as tie path. The nine-law pilot is transitive with score histogram `{0:1,...,8:1}`, `c3=0`, singleton SCCs, and one Hamiltonian path; next step is a two-coordinate observable combining cancellation with root/support compatibility. Status: METHOD CONFIRMED on pilot; math content OPEN. File: `HYP-2427-sign-law-tournament-analysis-quotient.md`.

- **HYP-2428 (eta powers form a sparsity-to-modularity cancellation ladder):** `eta^1` is Euler pentagonal sparse, `eta^3` is Jacobi triangular sparse, and `eta^24=Delta/q` is dense but modularly controlled. Stored window through `q^120`: support densities `18/121`, `16/121`, `68/121`, `121/121` for powers `1,3,8,24`; Jacobi eta^3 formula verified. Status: CONFIRMED pilot identities / OPEN proof lens. **HYP-2293 (REFUTED).** Conjectured Gstar(S)>=1/n (same floor as observer LRC, >> naive pair-count floor 1/(C(n-1,2)+1)). FALSE. First exact counterexample: V=(2,3,4,6,8) (gcd 1, n=6) has Gstar=3/19=0.1579 < 1/6=0.1667 (best cut A={2,3,4},B={6,8}, D={1,1,2,2,8,9,10,10,11,12}); verified exact (16 cuts) + independent float grid N=5e6. S711 lowers the bounded n=6 minimum further to 2/13 over B<=10, attained by (1,4,8,9,10), (2,3,7,9,10), (2,4,5,9,10), and finds the first bounded n=7 failure: (1,2,4,6,7,8) with Gstar=4/29<1/7 over B<=8. All currently known bounded failures lie in the NO-N-CUT class and each contains a residue contradiction motif a,a,-a mod n (n=6: 2,2,4 or the self-negative 3,3; n=7: 1,1,6). This motif forces the n-grid witness to fail, but it is NOT sufficient for below-floor: already at n=4,5 many no-n-cut sets remain strictly above 1/n, so the residue quotient captures only the on-grid obstruction.
**OPEN (T764):** what is inf_S Gstar(S) as a function of n? Current bounded minima: n=6 has min <= 2/13 over B<=10; n=7 has min <= 4/29 over B<=8. Characterize which no-n-cut residue obstructions force genuine below-floor behavior rather than merely shifting the witness off the n-grid. Tight sets (Gstar=1/n exactly) still suggest a consecutive-block / pairwise-worry-set story: (1,5,7,9) at n=5; (1,2,3,6,8),(1,2,4,5,6),... at n=6; (1,2,3,5,6,7),(1,2,4,5,6,7),(1,3,4,5,6,7) at n=7.

## HYP-2650: LRC(14) dyadic-richness as consec-maximality mechanism ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â REFUTED as primary, CONFIRMED as tiebreaker (kind-pasteur-2026-06-19-S13)
- **HYP-2650a (dyadic-richness maximizes p_0 = meas(S7) ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â REFUTED):** The hypothesis "p_0 is maximized by the speed set with the MOST dyadic doubling structure" is FALSE. - **HYP-2650b (CONTIGUITY is the primary driver ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â CONFIRMED):** max-consecutive-run is the strongest single correlate of p_0 (Pearson +0.268 vs richness +0.156). Mean p_0 by run-length is flat (~0.15) until run>=6, then jumps: run=6 mean 0.165, run=7 mean 0.282, run=8 mean 0.335. consec wins because it is the unique full-window (run=8).
- **HYP-2650c (dyadic-richness is the EXACT TIEBREAKER within near-consec ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â CONFIRMED, the clean find):** Within fixed-contiguity strata, the richness correlation STRENGTHENS as contiguity rises: run=6 +0.746, run=7 +0.828, run=8 +0.983. Within the run=8 (consec-shifted window) family, dyadic richness orders p_0 essentially monotonically, and is UNIQUELY maximized by the window starting at 1 (which alone contains the full power-of-2 chain {1,2,4,8}). Windows {1..8}/{2..9}/{3..10}/... have b=1 chain lengths 4/3/2/... and p_0 0.4162/0.3603/0.3369/... So: among maximally-contiguous sets, "start at 1" = "max power-of-2 chain" = max p_0.
- **HYP-2650d (doubling-monotonicity ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â CONFIRMED exhaustively, local-optimality certificate):** Replacing ANY single element of consec{1..k} by a larger unrelated value (breaking dyadic chains) STRICTLY decreases p_0. Exhaustive: k=8 gives 40/40 strict decreases, k=9 gives 36/36. This is a rigorous local-max certificate for consec under single-swaps. Worst-case sector-miss is 6 for all sets (the orbit always degenerates near x->0), so p_0 differences are global-volume, not worst-case, phenomena.
- **VERDICT:** The Glaisher/dyadic lens does NOT supply the maximization principle (contiguity does), but it DOES supply the correct ordering among the contenders that matter (near-AP windows), which is exactly the regime where the margin is tight (0.0014). The ergodic equidistribution intuition is suggestive but the controlling variable is the b=1 power-of-2 chain length, refining "start at 1 = AP" combinatorially. ## HYP-2718: LRC(14) carrier-product gap is a factorial-origin atom target (codex-2026-06-21)
- **THM-561 (proved basis theorem):** for any random missed-sector set `M subset U`, `Z_j=sum_{|R|=j}Pr(R subset M)=E[binom(|M|,j)]`.  Binomial inversion gives `Pr(|M|=t)=sum_{j>=t}(-1)^(j-t)binom(j,t)Z_j`; in particular `Pr(|M|=0)=sum_j(-1)^jZ_j`.  This is the normalized falling-factorial basis `(T)_j/j!`, equivalently a rising factorial basis in `-T`.
- **HYP-2718a (LRC translation):** for the actual-vs-product split-row comparison, `W_j=Delta E[binom(T,j)]` and `Q_t=Delta Pr(T=t)` obey `Q_t=sum_{j>=t}(-1)^(j-t)binom(j,t)W_j`.  Therefore `ProductCover-p0=Q_0=M_6`, the same scalar as HYP-2716's top Krawtchouk character, now interpreted as the origin atom after a finite-difference transform.

## HYP-2812: LRC(14) -- the R-tail Mordell-Tornheim constant is EXACTLY T=12*zeta(3) (closed form, makes HYP-2808 rigorous) (mac-mini-2026-06-22-S22)
Completes the analytic rigor of opus's HYP-2808 (R-tail = Mordell-Tornheim double sum). The owner's paper arXiv:2409.19980 (Matsumoto-Onodera-Sahoo, Mordell-Tornheim multiple zeta-functions + integral analogues via Abel summation) is exactly the right machinery; here the relevant constant evaluates in CLOSED FORM.
- **THE CONSTANT (PROVED):** T = sum_{h,h'!=0, h+h'!=0} 1/(|h||h'||h+h'|) = **12*zeta(3)** = 14.4247.... Derivation by sign-component reduction to the classical Mordell-Tornheim T(1,1,1): (++)=(--) = sum_{m,n>=1} 1/(mn(m+n)) = 2*zeta(3) each (Tornheim 1950); (+-)=(-+) = sum_{m!=n>=1} 1/(mn|m-n|) = 2*sum_{m>n} 1/(mn(m-n)) = 2*sum_{n,k>=1} 1/((n+k)nk) [m=n+k] = 2*(2*zeta(3)) = 4*zeta(3) each. T = 2*2zeta(3) + 2*4zeta(3) = 12*zeta(3). Numerics: direct N=4000 sum = 14.396 -> converges up to 12*zeta(3)=14.4247.
- **CONSEQUENCE for HYP-2808/THM-564 (rigor upgrade):** opus's R-tail bound |R_g| <= (1/pi^3)*T*(#arcs) is now CLOSED-FORM RIGOROUS: per-arc = 12*zeta(3)/pi^3 = 0.4654, <=12 arcs => |R_g| <= 144*zeta(3)/pi^3 = 5.583 (matches opus's empirical ceiling ~5.5; sup observed 2.244). So the R-tail's ABSOLUTE base-independent constant is no longer empirical -- it is 12*zeta(3), a classical Mordell-Tornheim value. Leg-C cutoff M* = ceil(G/(cap-Phi)) with G = period-max + |R| uses this rigorous constant.
- **PAPER LEAD (arXiv:2409.19980):** its integral analogue + Abel-summation asymptotics at x=0 could give an even SHARPER (integral) R_g bound than the per-arc 12*zeta(3)/pi^3, and its polylog relations may close-form the sharp sup (2.244) directly. Worth mining for the tight constant. -> HYP-2808, THM-564, HYP-2807, HYP-2792.

## HYP-3415: THE CRITICAL-PATH MAP -- LRC(14) needs exactly ONE new theorem beyond LRC<=13: the decorrelation floor (a single SPEC inequality).   (1) **Non-covering is ELEMENTARY and DONE.** For any S with q(S)=min{d: no multiple of d in S} <= 14, the q-witness t=1/q(S) gives f_S(1/q) = min_s ||s/q|| >= 1/q(S) >= 1/14 (each s not divisible by q => s mod q in {1..q-1} => ||s/q||>=1/q). So **the entire census (which 14-free sets are tight) is OFF the critical path** -- it characterizes EQUALITY (M=1/14), which the LRC INEQUALITY (M>=1/14) never needs. Two sessions of census/equioscillation/Galois work (HYP-3246..3413) are mathematically beautiful but a SIDE-QUEST for the inequality.
  (2) **Only the covering case (q(S)>=15) remains**, and it is INDUCTIVE. Covering => S has a multiple of every d<=14 => S = R (14-free, 13-r speeds) U 14Q (r>=1 multiples of 14). Under u=14t the multiples 14Q become a sub-LRC for Q (r<=6 runners), LONELY by LRC<=13 (the induction hypothesis). R is 14-free (q-witness safe). So LRC(14)-covering = LRC<=13(Q) + the DECORRELATION that R-safe and Q-lonely OVERLAP.
  (3) **The decorrelation is ONE inequality.** meas(R-safe AND Q-lonely) = sum_k ghat(k) Rhat_safe(14k) (Q-lonely is 1/14-periodic in t = g(14t)); the k=0 term = meas(R-safe)*meas(Q-lonely) (the product), so loneliness <=> R' = 1 + SPEC/product > 0, SPEC = sum_{k!=0} ghat(k) Rhat_safe(14k). **The whole LRC(14) reduces to: |SPEC| < product, uniformly over covering S.** This is exactly mac-mini's R'>=0.642 (HYP-3129, certified) + the resonant-v residual (S81/S82, off-grid bulk). The resonance = R's spectral overlap with the 14-grid = R's 2-adic/7-adic alignment (CRT 14=2*7); the apex-7 alignment is the resonant survivor mac-mini handles off-grid.
  THE HIGH-LEVERAGE CONCLUSION: **LRC(14) needs exactly ONE new theorem beyond LRC<=13 -- the uniform decorrelation floor |SPEC|<product (equivalently R'>=c>0).** Everything else is elementary (q-witness) or inductive (LRC<=13). All the structural beauty (census, equioscillation, Q(sqrt-7)/Q(cos2pi/7)/Galois, the H=7 lift) is either off-path or a tool for THIS one inequality.   (2) **The binding obstruction is the EVEN (2-adic) speeds.** At the M(S) optimum over 300 covering S, the binding (min-achieving) speeds are predominantly EVEN (376) vs ODD (279); the optimum is near t=1/2 only 58/300 times -- the even speeds PULL the witness off 1/2 (where the odd speeds would be happiest). The odd R-speeds are essentially FREE (lonely at 1/2); the 7-multiples and 14Q are LARGE and slack. So the floor's difficulty is the 2-PART of 14, not the 7-part.

The TIGHT/non-covering regime (the census, equioscillation, units mod 14, Q(sqrt-7), Galois C_6 -- HYP-3246..3413) is governed by the APEX 7 and is OFF the critical path.
